title: Why Pipe Sizing Matters for Water Pressure
description: Ever noticed your shower pressure plummet when someone flushes a toilet or starts the washing machine? The culprit is often improper pipe sizing. A home's plumbing system relies on calculated flow rates and water velocity. If main supply lines are undersized—such as using 1/2-inch pipe where a 3/4-inch main trunk line is required—water volume becomes severely restricted when multiple fixtures run simultaneously. On the drainage side, oversized pipes lack sufficient water velocity to scour solids away, leading to persistent clogs. Correct pipe sizing keeps water pressure consistent, prevents noisy water hammer, and protects your fixtures for years to come.
